newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. urges U.N. council not to condemn Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges U.N. council not to condemn Israel.

text.p: The United States urged fellow members of the U.N. Security Council on Friday to avoid condemnation of Israel over the Palestinian-Israeli crisis, saying it would not help the situation.

The appeal came from U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, Madeleine Albright, at a meeting of the Security Council. Washington is Israel's chief ally but many other countries have criticised the right-wing Israeli government.
"Let us turn our attention not toward condemnation, but toward encouraging the parties to restore the peace process and return to efforts to achieve concrete progress," Albright told the council.

The United States, which has led Middle East peace efforts for the last five years, has said it is trying to broker an end to the violence in the West Bank and Gaza in which more than 60 people have been killed.
"The members of this council should focus on how to help, how to restore calm, how to encourage the peace process...Words here are no substitute for action in the region," Albright said.
"Rhetoric offers them (the victims) no comfort. It does not advance the cause of peace."
